correlates.name: Reflex incontinence
correlates.presentation: A 36-year-old man 8 months after a T8 spinal cord injury from a motorcycle crash empties his bladder suddenly and without any warning sensation several times a day; he cannot tell when it is about to happen. Spastic legs; sensation absent below the nipples.
correlates.workup: Urodynamics: the bladder contracts on its own at low volume with no sensation of filling and no voluntary inhibition; postvoid residual varies.

correlates.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old man has 2 years of hesitancy, a weak stream, dribbling at the end, getting up 3 times a night, and sudden needs to void that sometimes leak before he reaches the toilet. Afebrile. Rectal exam: a smooth, symmetric, enlarged, rubbery, nontender gland.
correlates.workup: Urinalysis normal; postvoid residual 180 mL. Cystoscopy: the bladder wall is thickened, with coarse ridges of hypertrophied muscle bundles and a few small outpouchings.

correlates.name: Vesicovaginal or ureterovaginal fistula
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old woman, 3 weeks after an abdominal hysterectomy, is wet all the time, day and night: urine drips continuously with no urge and no relation to coughing or lifting. She still voids some urine normally. Afebrile; no flank pain.
correlates.management: Largely preventable at surgery: identify the ureters and take the bladder down during hysterectomy or C-section. These rarely arise on their own - a constantly wet patient after pelvic surgery or trauma is this until proved otherwise.

correlates.name: Cauda equina syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old warehouse worker has had 2 days of low back pain after lifting; today shooting pain and weakness in both legs, numbness of the buttocks, perineum and inner thighs, and he has leaked urine and stool without noticing. Ankle jerks absent bilaterally.
correlates.management: A medical and surgical emergency: recognize it early and arrange emergent spine imaging and surgical decompression the same day; delay risks permanent leg, bladder and bowel deficits.

correlates.name: Nocturnal incontinence in an older adult (fluid shifts)
correlates.presentation: A 79-year-old woman with heart failure and swollen ankles takes her furosemide at bedtime and drinks two cups of tea after dinner. She wakes 3-4 times a night to void and has started wetting the bed. Dry and in control by day. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin.
correlates.workup: Voiding diary: most of the 24-hour urine volume is passed between bedtime and morning; urinalysis normal; postvoid residual 40 mL; Na+ 138.
correlates.management: Last drink well before bed, no caffeine; move the diuretic to the morning; elevate the legs in the late afternoon and use support hose; review medications. Desmopressin only with caution: hyponatremia in the elderly can mean admission.

correlates.name: Urinary retention
correlates.presentation: A 76-year-old woman was started on oxybutynin for frequent voiding 3 days ago. For 14 hours she has passed no urine and has painful lower abdominal swelling. Afebrile; BP 158/90. Lower abdomen distended, tender above the pubis, dull to percussion up toward the umbilicus.
correlates.workup: Bladder ultrasound: 1,100 mL in the bladder; creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (0.9 baseline); urinalysis normal.
correlates.management: Decompress the bladder with a urethral catheter now and stop the anticholinergic (alpha agonists and calcium channel blockers do this too); admit when an obstructed bladder needs a catheter.
